BurlingtonJunior School
Vision, Mission and Values>
Vision, Mission and Values
‘Building foundations for life’
Our Vision
Burlington Junior School aims to inspire each individual child on their educational journey towards a lifelong love of learning and knowledge.
Our Mission
Staff are committed to:
Our Values
BELONG We all belong to our school community and work together to celebrate, respect and embrace our diversity.
JOY We know that children thrive both physically, mentally and emotionally when they are happy and safe.
SUCCEED All children have opportunities to succeed in every aspect of school life.

BurlingtonJunior School
Our Curriculum>
British Values
At Burlington Junior School, we have three shared values:
These values encourage our school community to consider how they can develop a personal sense of belonging, joy and success whilst at school, but also their responsibility to enable others to achieve this too.
What are British Values?
At Burlington Junior School, we promote the following fundamental British values as part of our pupils' spiritual, moral, social and cultural (SMSC) education:
This learning takes place in cross-curricular lessons and is not limited to specific SMSC lessons. We teach British values through a range of curriculum lessons (e.g. history), school assemblies, talks from guests who visit school and through day-to-day discussions with children. Our SMSC policy provides more information about how British values are addressed throughout daily school life.
Please follow the link below to go to the government website, for more information:
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/promoting-fundamental-british-values-through-smsc
democracy;
the rule of law;
individual liberty;
British Value: Democracy
Understanding democracy involves learning how decisions are made together, sharing that everyone has a voice, and understanding that everyone’s opinions and ideas matter. At school, children are encouraged to express their views, listen to others and understand that decisions are often made through discussion and voting. We help pupils understand the importance of fairness, participation and respecting the choices of others.
Children are encouraged to use their voices and make a positive contribution to the life of the school and the wider community through our School Council. Each class votes for their school councillors and these class representatives are able to take ideas from their class to School Council meetings where they are shared and discussed.
Other leadership opportunities for children include House Captains, Eco-Councillors, Sports Leaders and Junior Librarians. Children also have the opportunity to take on additional responsibilities within their classrooms, by becoming monitors, for example.
Democracy is one of our Burlington Buzz words and the concept is explored within and across year groups and subject areas.
Click here to read more about the work of our School Council.
British Value: The Rule of Law
The rule of law means understanding that rules and laws help to keep everyone safe and ensure that people are treated fairly. Children learn why rules are important, how they protect our rights and what can happen when rules are not followed. We encourage pupils to make responsible choices and understand the difference between right and wrong.
Our relational behaviour policy promotes the concepts of being ready, being respectful and being safe. Developing pupils' understanding of these principles within our school context ensures pupils feel safe and respected at school. They are then able to apply this understanding to knowledge of legislation within the wider world through assemblies and PSHE lessons.
British Value: Individual Liberty
Individual liberty means having the freedom to make choices and express yourself while understanding that our choices should not harm or unfairly affect others. We encourage children to develop confidence, independence and the ability to make informed decisions. Pupils learn that with freedom comes responsibility for their own actions and behaviour.
Through PSHE lessons, pupils learn about rights and responsibilities. These concepts are also explored through our assemblies.
British Value: Mutual Respect for and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs, and for those without faith.
In order for our pupils to feel a sense of belonging in school, we ensure pupils follow the behaviour principles of ready, respectful and safe. Everyone within our school community is unique and deserves to be treated with kindness, dignity and consideration. We teach children to listen to others, value different opinions and celebrate the qualities that make each person special. Pupils learn that respectful relationships help everyone feel safe, valued and included.
Tolerance means understanding and respecting people whose faiths, beliefs, cultures or backgrounds may be different from our own. We provide opportunities for children to learn about a range of beliefs and traditions, encouraging curiosity and open-mindedness. Pupils are taught that we can have different beliefs while living and learning together respectfully.
Our PSHE and R.E. curriculums enable these values to be explored as part of the curriculum; however, ensuring that all stakeholders feel a sense of belonging and respect is part of our core ethos here at Burlington. These values are therefore addressed and revisited on a regular basis.
Please follow the link below to go to the government website, for more information:
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/promoting-fundamental-british-values-through-smsc

BurlingtonJunior School
Acorns Breakfast and After School Club>
Acorns Breakfast and After School Club
At Acorns, we aim to provide a safe, secure and relaxed environment, offering a range of activities to reflect the interests of the children in our care. There will always be a selection of activities and resources available, including board games, construction toys, physical play, craft, cookery and reading.
Breakfast club is open from 7.30am weekdays during term time.
The After School club is open from 3.25pm until 6.30pm weekdays during term time. (Please note on school early-closure days, Acorns will close at 5.00 pm).
Admission
Admission to the clubs is for children who are 7 to 11 years old. Please click here to email for admission enquiries. We use a waiting list system when the need arises. The waiting list will be operated on a first come-first served basis, with the exception of siblings who will have priority for the same days as a sibling already attending.
We require a completed set of registration forms for each child before they can attend the club. Re-enrolment for September is required at the end of the summer term although existing club users will be given priority. We cannot keep a place open for your child unless you complete a new registration form each year.
Enquiries and Booking Requests
If you would like more information or to enquire about a booking please email the Junior Acorns Administrator at acorns@burlingtonjunior.org.
If Acorns is unable to offer your child a place, or you require alternative wraparound care, please visit the following pages for more information about local providers:
Achieving for Children's Childcare Search
Achieving for Children's Family Information Service
Fees
The current fees (from September 2025) are £6.50 per child per session for Breakfast Club and £15.50 per session for After School Club payable in advance.
This is payable for all booked sessions including when your child is sick, or on holiday (regardless of the amount of notice given). We do not charge for bank holidays and professional training days. When school closes early from 1.45pm (parents evening/end of term) the club will run from the end of the day until 5pm.
Parents are able to pay with electronic childcare vouchers and online via School Gateway. Please ensure that fees are paid promptly. Non-payment for more than one week may result in your place being terminated. If you are having difficulty paying fees, please speak in confidence to Sarah (Acorns Administrator) via email to acorns@burlingtonjunior.org.
Meals
Our menus are fully compliant with school food plan guidelines and are also mindful of any allergies/intolerances registered users may have. We recognise the importance of healthy nutrition for children delivered in a calm, friendly setting and request that food be consumed whilst sitting at the table.
Children are served breakfast from 7.30am-8.20am and are offered a choice of wholegrain cereals, toast and milk or water.
Our caterers Nourish are providing a full menu for the children’s evening meal. Fresh drinking water is available at all times. A hot meal will be served from 4.15.
Click here for the evening menu.
We are pleased to inform you that we received a Food Hygiene Rating of 5 from The Food Standards Agency (11/02/25)
The highest rating given, well done Acorns team!
Staff
All of our staff have experience of working with children and will undertake professional development training. All staff members are DBS checked.

Our Curriculum>
French
French is taught with a practical and creative approach at Burlington Junior School through the five pillars of phonology, grammar, vocabulary, culture, and songs, stories and rhymes. We encourage the children to develop a passion and enthusiasm for languages through song, role-play and games.
By regularly revising and reviewing prior learning, we ensure that pupils gain a solid foundation of language skills for them to build on each year. Our pupils develop their intercultural understanding by applying their learning to ‘real-life’ contexts.
“I went to Paris on a recent holiday and was able to speak to people in French!”
“It’s fun having conversations [in French] with each other, learning all together and we help each other.”
Our French Learning Journey
Our French learning journey works alongside the National Curriculum as well as taking into consideration the children's previous learning in Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2, and their future learning in Key Stage 3. This allows the children to build on their prior knowledge and skills whilst also preparing them for language lessons in secondary school.
"I love the interactive slides, singing songs in French and recapping what we have learned every week as it helps me to remember."
Enrichment in French and Modern Foreign Languages
Pupils have opportunities to participate in language competitions and events throughout the academic year including the Kingston and Merton Modern Foreign Languages Competition.
There are also additional practice tasks that pupils can complete in French, including our 'French Takeaway' worksheets to develop vocabulary. Pupils also have access to the Language Angels' Home School which pupils can log in to at home to further develop their skills in French.
“I like hearing a French person speaking when you press the speaker button in the lesson.”
"My favourite thing about French lessons is learning new words then trying to use them in full sentences."

Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE)
RSHE (Relationships, Sex and Health Education) sits within the Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE) Curriculum. High-quality, evidence-based and age appropriate teaching of RSHE supports children with emotional, social and cultural development, and involves learning about the important an important aspect of life: forming safe, positive and supportive relationships.
Statutory guidance from the Department for Education outlines what schools must teach within Key Stage Two. This includes teaching about the following themes:
Relationships Education
Physical Health and Mental Wellbeing
Sex education is not compulsory in primary schools, but we recommend that primaries teach sex education in years 5 and/or 6, in line with content about conception and birth, which forms part of the national curriculum for science. (DfE 2025) Please scroll down to read more about how sex education is taught at Burlington Junior School.
At Burlington Junior School, we make use of the Jigsaw programme to support our teaching of PSHE and RSHE. To find out more about this, please click on the icon below:
To find out more, please read our RSHE Policy, which you can find here.
To read more about the statutory guidelines for schools from the Department for Education, please click here.
Sex Education at Burlington Junior School
All pupils at Key Stage Two must be taught the aspects of sex education outlined in the primary science curriculum - this includes teaching about the main external parts of the human body, how it changes as it grows from birth to old age, including puberty, and the reproductive process in some plants and animals.
In Key Stage Two, within the National Curriculum for Science, pupils must be taught to:
According to statutory guidance from the DfE, the school is free to determine whether pupils should be taught sex education beyond what is required of the National Curriculum. At Burlington, we do teach pupils sex education within Year 5 and 6. The age and development of pupils is always considered when delivering sex education and we make use of age-appropriate resources from the Jigsaw scheme of work when planning and preparing materials for pupils.
Please see the learning journey below for more information about what is covered as part of pupils' learning about puberty (statutory health education) and non-statutory sex education lessons about conception. As a school, we are deeming the content which is highlighted in yellow as sex education because it covers human reproduction. Children can be withdrawn from lessons which cover the sections highlighted in red text. Please see our RSHE Policy for more information.

Our Curriculum>
Religious Education (R.E.)>
Religious Education (R.E.)
Through R.E., children will develop a deeper understanding of world religions, preparing them well for life in modern Britain, where British values are upheld and where people live alongside others from different faiths and cultures with respect and tolerance.
“I enjoy R.E lessons because I can learn about other religions and learn about my religion too.”
“I enjoy R.E because I love learning about different religions and how they worship and how they celebrate.”
Our R.E. Learning Journey
The school has no affiliation with any religion but follows the Kingston Agreed Syllabus for Religious Education. This syllabus aims to help children develop their knowledge and understanding of Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Judaism and non-religious beliefs and concepts.
Some year groups also have a series of lessons taught by Insight, a Christian group, who support Kingston schools.
Throughout their time at Burlington Junior School, pupils participate in a number of workshops and assemblies which enhance pupils' learning about different religions. This includes a Diwali workshop in Year 4, assemblies about different religious festivals and visits to local places of worship of different faiths.
In the classroom, pupils are encouraged to share their own experiences of religious festivals and celebrations with their classes.
“It is fun to learn about festivals in different countries/religions. I also enjoyed being an expert in Hinduism.”
